title: Resume partially completed rename undo
summary: Make multi-path rename undo durably resumable after a mid-sequence filesystem failure without reconstructing paths manually.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W04-004. Rename undo currently records only run-level state, so one committed reversal followed by a later failure leaves a mixed layout that the next strict preflight rejects.
behavior_before: Undo requires the entire original forward-renamed layout, mutates paths sequentially without per-operation checkpoints, and cannot retry after any operation succeeds before a later failure.
behavior_after: Each undo operation has an identity-bound prepared/committed checkpoint. Retry reconciles only exact forward, reversed, or same-file layouts, promotes a filesystem reversal whose checkpoint was lost, skips committed work, and resumes remaining operations without weakening collision or boundary checks.
tests_added: A deterministic sharing-violation fixture fails after one sidecar reversal, verifies its committed checkpoint, retries, skips that path, reverses the remaining media path, and compares content hashes.
A persistent manifest-checkpoint outage leaves the filesystem reversal ahead of its prepared record; restart reconciles the exact layout and completes safely.
A legacy failed manifest with no progress journal resumes from its exact mixed layout, preserving recovery for already-stranded manifests.
Progress identity tampering and a false committed status against a forward layout both fail before mutation.

rollback_plan: Revert the operation-level undo journal/resume logic, focused synthetic filesystem tests, generated context, and packet metadata together; retain the packet as incomplete evidence if rollback occurs.
notes: High-risk rename mutation boundary. The strict confirm_apply contract, configured-root authority, collision checks, metadata-backup boundaries, and reverse execution order remain intact. Existing atomic manifest writes now checkpoint operation identities and committed state. Representative synthetic media/sidecar files, injected failures, restart/resume, and content hashes are required; real-media decoding is not required by the audit rung.
